items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to business protection
for point-of-sale equipment leases
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S540

SPONSOR: THOMAS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to business
protection for point-of-sale equipment leases

 
PURPOSE:

To regulate leases of credit card terminals to merchants and curb unfair
practices by finance leasing companies.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill adds a new article 42 to the general business law
titled, "credit card terminal leases."

Section 1100 defines credit card terminal and requires salespeople to
disclose, orally and in writing, to prospective lessees the nature of
their relationship to entities that own, lease, service, and finance the
credit card terminal and the terms of the finance lease and whether oral
statements or commitments made by the salesperson are included in the
finance lease and enforceable. The written disclosure given to a
prospective lessee must be in at least twelve point font, in the primary
language used to communicate with the prospective lessee, and in the
same or similar language used by the salesperson when soliciting the
lease.

Section 1101 requires finance leases to be drafted in plain language and
disclose the terms, total price, total monthly payment, whether the
credit card terminal can be purchased and at what price, and contact
information for all parties involved in the leasing, servicing, and
financing of the credit card terminal. If the contact information
provided to the lessee changes, the lessee must be notified of the
change within five business days. The finance lease must also include a
provision that caps the total cost the lessee is required to pay at
three hundred percent of the lessor's original purchase price for the
credit card terminal.

An agreement for the delivery of services for a credit card terminal
must be included in a service agreement separate from the finance lease.
A service agreement must disclose the terms governing the delivery of
services, the total price for services, the total monthly payment, and
any penalties or fees and conditions under which they can be incurred.

The finance lease and the service agreement must both state any discount
for bundling the credit card terminal lease and delivery of services and
the cost for bundled and unbundled packages.

Lessors must provide copies of the executed lease to the lessee, retain
copies of the executed lease, and retain proof that the executed lease
reached the lessee. Lessors must allow a lessee to cancel a lease within
45 days of receiving a copy of the executed lease. Cancellation fees are
limited to the total monthly payment disclosed to the lessee in the
finance lease. A lessee is not required to pay a cancellation fee if
there is evidence of fraud or illegality. Lessors cannot include
provisions in a finance lease that designate a judicial forum to hear
disputes that would not otherwise have jurisdiction over the lessee.
Section 1102 states that a violation of this article is a violation of
the state deceptive act or practice law found in Article 22-A of the
general business law.

Section 2 authorizes the Attorney General to promulgate any rules or
regulations necessary to implement this act.

Section 3 of the bill states the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Equipment leasing is a valuable tool for business owners who would
otherwise need to borrow or invest in the purchase of such equipment.
The convenience of leasing equipment is offset by the fact that the
business is paying much more over time to lease the equipment than it
would have cost to purchase the equipment outright. Predatory finance
leasing companies further take advantage of business owners by locking
them into mandatory 4 year leases, preventing the business from cancel-
ing leases, misrepresenting key terms of the lease, and including unfair
forum selection clauses in the leases.

In New York, the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) pursued an action
against Northern Leasing Systems, Inc. for repeated and persistent
fraud. Some of the deceptive business practices outlined by the OAG
against Northern Leasing Systems included: targeting small, family-owned
businesses, prohibiting them from reviewing the financing leases, not
providing copies of the financing lease, being unreachable to consumers,
and using alternate service provisions and forum selection clauses to
abuse the judicial process.

The OAG reported that businesses made 1,643 complaints to the Office
between January 1, 2010 and December 31, 2015. During that same period,
Northern Leasing Systems filed more than 30,000 actions in New York
County Civil Court and obtained more than 19,000 default judgments. The
exorbitant number of cases brought by Northern Leasing System required
the Civil Court to create a separate calendar part to hear only actions
brought by Northern Leasing.

The proposed legislation would address predatory practices in point of
sale equipment leases and prevent credit card leasing companies from
taking advantage of New York businesses by ensuring that businesses have
more information about the terms of a credit card terminal lease, the
cost of the equipment and the opportunity to cancel the lease.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-22: S.7748 (Thomas) / A.8593 (Fall) - Referred to Consumer
Protection.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Enacts provisions relating to the lease of credit card terminals; requires disclosures; prohibits certain practices.
title: Relates to business protection for point-of-sale equipment leases
